title: Fix path-traversal escape in safe_join
description: safepath.join.safe_join(base, *parts) must join parts under base but raise ValueError if the result escapes base (via '..' or an absolute component). It currently uses a naive posixpath.join that allows escape. Fix safepath/join.py using posixpath string logic only (NO real filesystem access). Do not modify any test files. Clarification: an absolute component in `parts` (e.g. "/etc/passwd") must be rejected with ValueError unconditionally -- not only when the final joined-and-normalized string happens to fall outside base. `posixpath.join` resets to an absolute component and discards every earlier component including base, so an absolute part is never actually joined under base regardless of where that absolute string itself points; a call such as `safe_join("/srv/data", "/srv/data/logs/app.log")` must still raise even though that absolute string happens to read as being inside base.
